chunks: From him, from al-Ḥasan ibn Maḥbūb, from Hishām ibn Sālim, from Ḥabīb al-Sijistānī, who said:

I asked Abā Jaʿfar عليه السلام about a man who cut off the right hands of two men. He said: “O Ḥabīb, his right hand is cut off for the one whose right hand he cut off first, and his left hand is cut off for the one whose right hand he cut off last, because he only cut off the hand of the latter man, while his right hand is retaliation for the first man.”

He said: So I said, “ʿAlī عليه السلام used only to cut off the right hand and the left foot.” He said: “He only used to do that in matters that are due in the rights of Allah. But as for what is due from the rights of the Muslims, their rights are taken for them in retaliation: the hand for the hand when the cutter has two hands, and the foot for the hand when the cutter does not have two hands.”

So I said to him, “Only blood-money is due from him, and his foot is left.” He said: “Blood-money is only due from him when he cuts off a man’s hand and the cutter has neither two hands nor two feet. In that case blood-money becomes due from him, because he has no limb from which retaliation can be taken.”

key_terms.الدِّيَةُ: financial compensation due when equivalent retaliation cannot be carried out
key_terms.الْقِصَاصِ: retaliatory legal retribution in bodily injury cases
key_terms.الْيَدُ بِالْيَدِ: the principle of equivalent retaliation by the same limb
key_terms.جَارِحَةٌ: a bodily limb or organ from which equivalent retaliation may be taken
key_terms.حُقُوقِ اللَّهِ: claims and penalties belonging to the divine legal order
key_terms.حُقُوقِ الْمُسْلِمِينَ: the personal legal rights of injured individuals that must be restored

ai.seo_question: How is qisas applied if someone cuts off the right hands of two different people?
ai.summary: This hadith explains rulings of qisas in cases of bodily injury, specifically when a person cuts off the right hands of two different men. It distinguishes between punishments related to the rights of Allah and retaliatory justice related to the rights of people, clarifying when a hand, foot, or blood-money is due.
